open_points.subject: _credential_is_usable
open_points.text: - _credential_is_usable: [BEHAVIOR] MUST be true only when credential and principal are active, the credential is unrevoked, and checked_at is before expires_at when present.
open_points.other_text: - ServiceCredential fields (exact, no others exist): created_at: datetime, created_by: UUID, credential_id: UUID, expires_at: datetime | None, key_version: int, revoked_at: datetime | None, revoked_by: UUID | None, secret_hash: str, service_principal_id: UUID
open_points.question: Must the requirement stop requiring an active credential, define activity solely through the declared revocation and expiry fields, or must ServiceCredential gain a status field?

open_points.subject: authenticate_service_principal
open_points.text: - authenticate_service_principal: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST open its transaction with an explicit assignment, never as a context manager, reach principal and credential persistence only through tx.service_identity(), use no legacy transaction-level service method, and close the transaction exactly once. It reads and writes nothing, so it rolls back once after its last read and never commits; a failure rolls back only while the local open flag still marks the transaction open.
open_points.other_text: - authenticate_service_principal: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST verify the selected credential secret, expiry, revocation, and active principal before returning trusted source_type, scope_mode, and key_version; failures reveal no selector state.
open_points.question: Does authentication read the selected credential and principal, or must it read nothing?

It reads and writes nothing, so it rolls back once after its last read and never commits; a failure rolls back only while the local open flag still marks the transaction open.

open_points.subject: change_service_principal_status
open_points.text: - change_service_principal_status: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST complete its authorization check before it opens a transaction, never while one is open, because the check opens a transaction of its own and a second one nested inside this transaction is forbidden. It MUST then open its transaction with an explicit assignment, never as a context manager, reach service principal, credential and producer-grant persistence only through tx.service_identity(), append audits only through tx.audit(), use no legacy transaction-level service method, and close the transaction exactly once: a successful write commits once, a failure rolls back only while the local open flag still marks the transaction open and re-raises the original failure unchanged.
